metadata.score_guide: HOW TO READ SUITABILITY SCORES: Each site carries one composite suitability score between 0 and 1. Higher is better. The score combines three service factors — building-footprint density as a population-demand proxy (weight 0.40), road accessibility (0.25) and distance from the nearest existing health facility as a coverage-gap term (0.15) — and then subtracts penalties for flood (0.08), landslide (0.07) and storm-surge (0.05) susceptibility. Hazard penalties are applied inside every score; there is no separate "with hazard" and "without hazard" result. Scores are rescaled across the study area, so they rank sites against one another rather than against an absolute standard. Sites are grouped into four classes: Not Suitable below 0.25, Low Suitability from 0.25 to 0.40, Moderately Suitable from 0.40 to 0.60, and Highly Suitable at 0.60 and above. Road accessibility is a normalized inverse distance: a value near 0 means the site is FAR from the mapped road network and therefore has LOW accessibility, while a value near 1 means it sits close to a road. Facility distance runs the other way: a larger distance marks a wider service gap and counts in a site’s favour. Any site within 50 m of the coastline is retained and displayed but is barred from the recommendation list, as is any site carrying a High hazard class.

dataset_clarification.note: 4,630 raw OpenStreetMap records — building footprints, road nodes, road edges and health facilities — were extracted for feature engineering. These are source records, not candidate locations. Feature engineering aggregates them onto a lattice of 3,119 candidate sites, which is the number of locations actually scored. 66 of those sites fall within the 50 m shoreline setback: they are scored and displayed but barred from the recommendation list.

metadata.advisory_note: POLARIS is an advisory decision-support tool. Its scores rank candidate locations on the spatial factors listed in the score guide and do not account for land tenure, acquisition cost, zoning, utility provision or community consultation. Final siting decisions rest with the City Health Office and the City Planning and Development Office.
